subtopics.title: Stretch One Dimension — Volume Follows It

questions.question: A box $4 \times 3 \times 2$ has its height doubled (now $4 \times 3 \times 4$). Its volume changes from 24 to:
Multiplying ONE dimension of a prism by k multiplies the volume by:
Why does surface area NOT simply double when only the height doubles?
options: Some faces contain the height and scale; the top and bottom do not, so the total scales by no clean factor
Surface area never changes under scaling
Because surface area always scales by $k^3$
Because the net becomes a different shape

questions.question: After doubling only the height of the $4 \times 3 \times 2$ box, the new surface area is:
A cylinder's radius is doubled, height unchanged. The volume multiplies by:
Why does k on the radius give $k^2$ on the cylinder's volume?
options: The radius is squared in $V = \pi r^2 h$, so it enters the product twice
It is a rounding effect of $\pi$

questions.question: Cylinder with $V = 300\pi$: triple the radius, keep the height. The new volume is:
Multiplying only the HEIGHT of a cylinder by k multiplies the volume by:
options: $k$, because h appears once in $\pi r^2 h$
